description: Add a bottleneck — a problem without solving which the game stalls. At least 3 independent solution paths are required. textId is unique, format [a-z0-9-]+. A repeat call with the same textId replaces the record. If the book has no bottlenecks — do NOT call addBottleneck, but call `completeTask("add-bottlenecks")` directly.
name: addBottleneck

textId.description: Slug identifier of the bottleneck, format [a-z0-9-]+.

problem.description: Bottleneck: a problem without which the game stalls. For example: "The party needs the key to the secret door", "the party must learn the traitor's name".

solutionPaths.description: At least 3 independent solution paths. For example: "(1) interrogate the captain, (2) steal the logbook, (3) talk to the victim's ghost". Each is self-contained, not a subset of another.

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description: Add a combat encounter — a battle with a list of participants and their compact stat blocks. textId is unique. Required for COMBAT nodes (otherwise the planner has to invent HP/AC on the fly). For MIXED — if there is a combat phase. Closes `add-encounters` on the first call.
name: addEncounter

name.description: Title (for analytics/UI): "Battle at the Crater's Edge", "Finale at the Anvil", "Ambush on the Way to the Island".

nodeTextId.description: textId of the node where it takes place. If null — the encounter is "floating", the planner can drop it in a suitable place.

description.description: Situation: who is here, what each side wants (a motive, not "they attack"), what will happen if the players do not intervene. 2-4 sentences.

idea.description: The battle's IDEA — the answer to "WHY does this battle exist at THIS point of the story": what is at stake, what the battle changes or reveals (the hero's arc, a twist, the price of a decision, the truth about the world). The setting, the enemy roster and spectacle are NOT the idea, they are decoration (`description` is about the SITUATION "who is here and what they want"; idea is about the MEANING of the battle in the plot). THE MAIN design field: the tactical question, the enemies' behavior and the stakes flow from the idea. An idea that is a scene description rather than a "why" → "a battle for the sake of a battle", a defect: perhaps the battle does not belong here.

participants.description: Encounter participants — enemies/neutral forces. At least 1.

profile.description: A profile WITHOUT NUMBERS: signature traits + relative danger in one or two phrases. "An elite shadow assassin — hits hard from stealth, fragile himself, relies on ambush". "A dim-witted brute — lots of health, slow, hits like a hammer". NO CR/HP/AC/damage — the turn master computes those to fit the party's strength.

scale.description: Relative scale of presence (NOT an absolute number): SOLO — a loner/boss; FEW — a small group; MANY — a noticeable crowd; SWARM — a swarm of minions. The exact number is chosen by the turn master to fit the player side's strength. Relative scale (no numbers): So=solo/boss; Fw=few/small group; Mn=many/crowd; Sw=swarm/swarm of minions.

role.description: Role in battle (exactly one word in Latin letters): "boss", "lieutenant", "minion", "support", "summon", "ally". This is the participant's canon, not an ornament: the turn master builds the enemy's role in battle from it, and "minion" is a minor role: a SWARM unit (one sheet represents a crowd) or a specific unit with its own role, not a clone extra. Set "minion" by its place in the battle, not as a filler by number.

motive.description: The participant's motive: what they want in this scene (besides "kill the heroes"). "Finish the ritual", "prevent escape", "hold out until help arrives", "protect the master". Makes behavior rounded, not just "attacks".

tacticalQuestion.description: **The main TACTICAL QUESTION** the battle puts to the player: "how to reach an enemy who is out of reach?", "how to protect an NPC while fighting?", "how to survive until reinforcements?". It is NOT the narrative reason for the battle ("bandits attacked") — it is the puzzle for the sake of which the battle exists. No tactical question → no battle is needed (reduce it to narrative/skip). Required (the validator rejects an empty one). See the "Battle construction" block.

primaryObjective.description: The party's main goal in the encounter beyond "kill everyone": disrupt a ritual, rescue captives, obtain an item, hold a position, win the crowd's favor. One sentence.

secondaryObjective.description: An additional optional objective (a tempting one): capture the lieutenant, obtain a document, keep an NPC from dying. Optional.

alternativeSolutions.description: At least 2 resolution paths besides combat: negotiation, deception, stealth, thwarting the plan, the environment, a bribe, a moral argument. Concrete, not "somehow get out of it".

terrain.description: Terrain with **four** traits: cover · movement obstacle · environmental hazard (hazards) · atmospheric detail. The best terrain contains all four.

tactics.description: **MUST BE FILLED IN** (null/blank is rejected by the validator). The opponents' tactics: how they fight, which combos they use, whom they attack first, at what HP they retreat/change behavior. 2-4 sentences, a description of behaviour, not a reactive strategy. Without tactics the encounter cannot be run by the turn master.

synergies.description: Explicit SYNERGIES between enemies "X reinforces Y" — where difficulty comes from (from the INTERACTION of roles, not from the sum of stat blocks): "the Controller roots the PC → the Artillery focuses them", "the Support enrages the Brute → an extra attack", "A places hazard terrain → B pushes into it with forced movement". Reference real participants by name/role. Two identical units are differentiated not by stats but by role (one holds the flank, the other pushes). NOT mechanically gated (a SOLO boss legitimately has no links) — checked by self-review. An empty list — only for solo bosses.

twist.description: Twist draft: reinforcements / a new danger / an unexpected reveal + a trigger condition. The generator writes a DRAFT — the decision to introduce it is made by the turn planner in real time. Optional.

event.description: What happens: enemy reinforcements, a roof collapse, a third party appearing, an ally's mask being revealed. 1-2 sentences.

trigger.description: Trigger condition: "the alarm is raised", "the battle lasts >5 rounds", "an NPC drops below 50% HP", "a rune is activated", "the party is close to victory". Precise at the end, so the planner understands when to introduce it.

stakes.description: Plot consequences of failure OUTSIDE the scene (not just a "rollback"): "the order's reputation falls", "the protagonist gets an artifact", "the village is left without protection", the BB speeds up the timeline. One concrete sentence. Differs from `lossCondition` (an observable trigger INSIDE the scene) — this is what will echo AFTER the battle.

lossCondition.description: The observable LOSS TRIGGER INSIDE the scene — a mechanical condition, and NOT necessarily a TPK: "the prisoner was carried out through the north exit", "the alarm is raised — reinforcements in 2 rounds", "the NPC ally was led away", "the party was bound and captured". Without a loss-condition the stakes are not real (the battle = an HP race to zero). Differs from `stakes` (consequences OUTSIDE the scene) — this is what fires RIGHT IN THE BATTLE. Required (the validator rejects an empty one).

arenaSupport.description: How the arena **physically supports** the primaryObjective. "An altar in the center with an approach from the right — for 'disrupt the ritual'", "4 doors on the perimeter — for 'hold the position'", "a staircase to the balcony for a stealthy flank". Optional (recommended for boss fights and important encounters). Linked via `nodeTextId → locationTextId`.

phases.description: Phases of a multi-phase battle (1c §3): "phase 1 — disable the shield, phase 2 — finish the boss", "ground → when the dragon is wounded, it flies off to a cliff, an aerial battle begins". Each phase has its own condition (when to switch) and effect (what changes). An empty list — a one-shot battle. Usually for boss fights and the climax.

name.description: Title: "Phase 1: disable the shield", "Phase 2: finish the boss", "Phase air: the dragon in the air", "Finale: forge collapse".

description.description: Phase description: what happens, what the task is, what the choices are. 1-3 sentences.

condition.description: Condition for transitioning into this phase. For the first — null/"battle start"; for subsequent ones — a concrete trigger: "when the boss's HP <50%", "when the shield crystal is destroyed", "after round 5", "when one of the minions ran off for reinforcements".

effect.description: What changes in the arena/encounter on switching: new opponents appear, hazards activate, access to a POI opens, terrain changes (the bridge collapsed). Concretely — what the planner must change in the scene.

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description: Add a hint/rumor/lore fragment — something the turn planner can drop to the players via an NPC, a book, an inscription. textId is unique. Category: RUMOR/LORE/WARNING/SECRET/OBJECTIVE. Closes the `add-hints` task on the first call.
name: addHint

textId.description: Slug identifier of the hint, format [a-z0-9-]+. For references from nodes/NPCs.

source.description: Source of the hint: "NPC <name>", "A book in the monastery", "A rumor in the tavern", "An old diary". Helps the planner choose how to present it.

content.description: The hint text itself — what the players will hear/read. Direct speech or a description of the content. 1-3 sentences.

category.description: Hint category (see [AiBookHintCategory]). Hint/lore fragment category: Rum=a rumor in public places (publicly available, may be embellished); Lor=knowledge about the world/history/rules (via an expert NPC or a book); Wrn=a warning about danger (what awaits around the corner, saves the inattentive); Sec=hidden information (behind a skill check, in a cache, in a secret room); Obj=a goal/quest hook ("X needs to be done", "the roads to Y go through Z").

relatedTextIds.description: textIds of the NPCs/nodes/items/encounters the hint relates to. Helps the planner understand when it is appropriate to present it (next to this entity).

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description: Add an item/loot/artifact. textId is unique. Must be bound either to a node (`nodeTextId`) or to an NPC (`npcTextId`) — not both null. Magical mechanics are optional (for ordinary gold — null). Closes `add-items` on the first call.
name: addItem

name.description: Title: "Ring of Acid Resistance", "Blueprint of a Spiked Shield", "3 Red-hot Stones", "150 gp", "Reputation at the Baron's Court".

category.description: Reward type-category (see [AiBookItemCategory]) — needed for the check "do not dump everything into gold". Item/loot category: Mon=coin (gold/silver/copper/jewels for sale, purchase flexibility); Mag=magical/mechanical item (weapon/armor/ring/consumable/scroll); Mun=ordinary mundane item (a key, a document, a tool, a blueprint, an artifact without magic); Nar=non-material reward (reputation, knowledge/secret, an NPC/faction service, access to a place, a title).

description.description: Description as a moment of the story: appearance, material, legend, feel. Not an inventory line but a trace in the fiction. 1-2 sentences.

sourceConnection.description: Binding to the source: why **this particular** item is with this NPC / in this node. "The ring came to the giant from the last city he burned", "the ritual scroll was on the cultist's person". Helps the planner present the find.

mechanics.description: D&D mechanics, if the item is magical: "+2 to hit/damage", "fire immunity for 1 minute", "can recall a 3rd-level spell". Null for ordinary items / non-material rewards.

nodeTextId.description: textId of the node where the item lies. Null if with an NPC. For non-material rewards (reputation/access) — the node where it is obtained.

npcTextId.description: textId of the NPC who holds the item / who gives the non-material reward. Null if in the node.

locationHint.description: A hint of where exactly / how it is discovered: "on the belt", "in the purse", "in a heap behind the stove", "chained to the anvil", "opens after a successful social check", "found when searching the body". Helps the planner describe the search.

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description: Add a key NPC. Each has: a name, a motive, one characteristic trait, an attitude toward the party, an attitude toward the BB. textId is unique in the format [a-z0-9-]+. A repeat call with the same textId replaces the record. Closes the `add-key-npcs` task when the first NPC is added.
name: addKeyNpc

textId.description: Slug identifier of the NPC, format [a-z0-9-]+. Used by the planner for references (`ml:character:textId`).

name.description: NPC name. Unique, localized to the generation language.

motive.description: Motive: what the NPC wants. May coincide with or conflict with the party's goal — this gives texture.

trait.description: Characteristic trait: one vivid detail of behavior/appearance/speech by which the NPC is remembered. Not a stat block description.

attitudeToParty.description: Attitude toward the party: "ally", "neutral", "suspicious", "hostile", with one sentence on why.

attitudeToAntagonist.description: Attitude toward the BB: "works for the BB under duress", "a victim", "does not know about the BB", "a rival", with one sentence on why.

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description: Write the SHELL of a key location: a space with a setting and optionally a text grid map. Do it only for important places: the final COMBAT arena (the map is required), the starting scene in a space, complex tactical nodes. A simple social scene/dialogue does not need a location. mode=CREATE — a new location (name, description, ambient are required); mode=UPDATE — editing an existing one, what is not sent does not change. POIs and hazards are not part of this: after CREATE add them one by one with addLocationPoi / addLocationHazard in the same response (the calls execute in order). CREATE closes the `add-locations` task.
name: addLocation

mode.description: CREATE — a new location (the textId is not yet taken); UPDATE — editing an existing location by location.textId

location.description: Location shell (textId, name, description, ambient, grid?, interactives?) — without POIs and hazards

textId.description: Slug identifier of the location, format [a-z0-9-]+. mode=CREATE — a new one (no such location yet); mode=UPDATE — an existing location.

name.description: Title: "Crater of the Star Forge", "The Baron's Throne Room". CREATE — required; UPDATE — do not send if you are not changing it.

description.description: General description of the space: what kind of place it is, what the players see right at the entrance. 2-4 sentences. CREATE — required; UPDATE — do not send if you are not changing it.

ambient.description: Atmosphere and physics: light, sound, smell, scale. CREATE — required; UPDATE — the object replaces ambient entirely, do not send if you are not changing it.

light.description: Lighting: "dusk", "bright daylight with dusty streaks", "dark, only torches by the doors", "pulsing light of rune columns".

sound.description: Sound background: "silence and dripping water", "the roar of machines and shouting", "distant chanting of monks", "crackling fire in the hearth".

smell.description: Smell (optional): "the smell of burnt metal and sweat", "ozone and perfume", "rotting seaweed". Helps immersion a lot.

scale.description: Scale/dimensions: "a hall 100×80 ft, ceiling 100 ft", "a cave 30×30 ft", "an open crater, diameter 300 ft". Helps the planner estimate distances for movement/spells.

grid.description: Text map (optional; for tactical locations). UPDATE — the object replaces the grid entirely; edit a single row with updateLocationGridRow, the legend with addLocationLegendEntry/removeLocationLegendEntry.

widthCells.description: Map width in cells = number of characters in each row.

heightCells.description: Map height in cells = number of rows.

mapGrid.description: Text map. One symbol = one cell. Rows are separated by a real newline (`\n` in a JSON-encoded string = a real newline character). The service automatically normalizes accidental double-escapes (a literal `\n`) and adjusts widthCells/heightCells to the actual grid. The map holds only static terrain and objects; mark the encounter participants' starting positions with a separate symbol + a legend entry with relatedTextId pointing to the participant.

legend.description: Legend: every symbol used in `mapGrid` is described by a separate entry. An entry has: name (a short name — for the UI/planner), description (a full description with mechanics), relatedTextId (optional — to an interactive/hazard/POI/participant).

symbol.description: Symbol — EXACTLY ONE character (a letter a-z/A-Z, a digit 0-9 or one of +-*=/|:;,~^@#%&). Case matters: 'H' and 'h' are different symbols. By itself it means nothing — the meaning is in `name`+`description`. Within one map a symbol must be unique; on different maps the same symbol may mean different things.

name.description: A short artistic caption for the PLAYER over the map (optional, STINGY — 0-4 per map): "Isolde's Altar", "Well", "Forge". ONLY for key visible buildings/objects. WITHOUT name: base terrain (floor/walls/water), decorative props, the HIDDEN (traps/caches — the caption would spoil them) and "starting positions" (the party's entry point is a property of the visit, settled by tokens, not by the map).

description.description: Full description with mechanical details: "a stone wall 5×5×10ft, AC 18, 20 HP, immune to poison and psychic, collapses when HP is lost", "an oil barrel — partial cover (+2 AC); when hit by fire it ignites in a 10ft radius for 3d6 fire". Must be enough for the turn planner to run the scene without consulting a PDF.

relatedTextId.description: textId of the related entity — if the symbol denotes an interactive (`location.interactives[].textId`), a hazard (`location.hazards[].textId`), a POI (`location.pointsOfInterest[].textId`) or an encounter participant. Null if the symbol denotes plain terrain (floor/wall/cover with no special rules).

cellSizeFeet.description: Size of one cell in feet. 5 by default (D&D standard). For large-scale maps (crater, battlefield) — 10/20 ft.

orientation.description: Orientation: "N=up", "entrance from the south". Optional, but desirable for battles where direction matters.

interactives.description: Interactive objects of the combat arena. CREATE — the initial list; UPDATE — the list replaces all interactives entirely, do not send if you are not changing it.

name.description: Title: "Oil Candelabra", "Bridge Support Chain", "Water Sluice Lever", "Alchemical Barrels", "Swinging Rope".

gridPosition.description: Position on the map: "row 5, col 12" or "x:12, y:5". If the object is spread out (wall/chain) — a zone description.

description.description: Description: what it is, what it looks like, what makes it noticeable. 1-2 sentences.

trigger.description: Activation trigger: what the player (or enemy) must do. "Cut the rope (Athletics DC 12)", "Atk +5 vs AC 13", "Set it on fire with a fire spell", "Push (Athletics DC 15)", "Use key X". Must be achievable in combat.

effect.description: Activation effect: what happens after the trigger. Concretely — DC/damage/area/timing. "The chandelier falls onto cells B3-D5, 22 (4d10) bludgeoning, DC 15 Dex saving throw for half", "The portcullis drops, blocking the south exit for 1 minute", "The barrels explode: 3d6 fire in a 10ft radius".

usableBy.description: Who can use it: PARTY (the party only), ENEMIES (the enemies only), BOTH (both sides — the enemies too can cut the chain to drop it on the party). Who can use an interactive object in the arena: Par=the party only (the heroes' lever), Ene=the enemies only (an enemy ritual/device), Bot=both sides (a shared lever/altar).

oneShot.description: Whether it is single-use (`true` — after activation the object is spent, for example a fallen chandelier) or can trigger repeatedly (`false` — a lever can be used several times).

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description: Add ONE environmental hazard to an existing location. The only way to record a hazard: addLocation has none. Editing a hazard — removeLocationHazard + addLocationHazard.
name: addLocationHazard

name.description: Title: "Acid Fumes", "Lava Field", "Floor Snare Trap", "Magical Sleep".

telegraph.description: Telegraph: a noticeable sign of danger **before the player steps in**. "The water is bright turquoise, acrid fumes", "cracks in the floor, a dark crust", "the hum is growing". Without it the danger turns into a "gotcha" — a punishment for the player's inattention.

trigger.description: Trigger condition: "a creature within 10ft of the water", "weight >100 pounds on the plate", "opening the door without dispelling the charm", "6+ rounds in the zone".

effect.description: Effect under targetLevel: "DC 15 Con save, 21 (6d6) acid damage on a failure, half on a success", "fall 30ft taking 10 (3d6) bludgeoning damage", "polymorph into a sheep for 1 hour".

waysToAvoid.description: At least 3 independent ways to detect/bypass/disarm. "Perception DC 12 to notice the cracks", "Detect Magic reveals the outline", "Jump over the zone (Athletics DC 14)", "Use the ring of resistance".

justification.description: Justification in the fiction: why the hazard is here — a link to the inhabitants' scheme, the nature of the place, history. "Acid seeps from a cracked rune stone under the star", "Brimskarda set it up to hold the dragon". Helps the planner fit it into the narrative.

escalation.description: Spread rule for escalating hazards (advancing water/fire/gas/collapse): "expands by 5ft each round", "doubles damage after round 3", "after 2 rounds the zone covers the whole map". Null — a static hazard. Creates time pressure in space: drives fighters into the desired zones.

escalationTrigger.description: Escalation start condition: "when the alarm is raised", "after round 3", "when the boss is below 50% HP", "when a column is broken". Null — the escalation is active from the start of the scene. Fill in if `escalation != null`.

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description: Add an entry to the location legend (one entity ↔ one symbol). Use before adding a symbol to mapGrid, otherwise validation will say the symbol is an orphan.
name: addLocationLegendEntry

symbol.description: Single-character symbol; must be unique in the legend

description.description: Description of the entity the symbol stands for

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description: Add ONE point of interest (POI) to an existing location. The only way to record a POI: addLocation has none. Editing a POI — removeLocationPoi + addLocationPoi.
name: addLocationPoi

textId.description: Slug identifier of the POI, format [a-z0-9-]+. Unique within the location.

label.description: Display label: "1", "A", "BOSS", "N". The same as in `grid.cells` if the POI is on the map.

name.description: POI name: "Broken Bridge", "Acid Lake", "Altar of Isolde".

description.description: Description: what the players see/find/can do. 2-5 sentences. Includes game-mechanical details (check DCs, effects) where appropriate.

gridPosition.description: Position on the map: "row 5, col 12" or "x:12, y:5". Null if the POI is not on the grid (for example, for a location without a grid).

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description: Add a node (location/scene/face). Each is a self-contained situation with a scene type and exit hints to other nodes. textId is unique, format [a-z0-9-]+. A repeat call with the same textId replaces the node. Closes the `add-nodes` task upon reaching ≥3 nodes.
name: addNode

textId.description: Slug identifier of the node, format [a-z0-9-]+. Used for references in `hintsOut`/`bottlenecks`.

title.description: Short node name for the index/UI: "The Abandoned Mill", "Interrogating the Guard Captain".

sceneType.description: Scene type: COMBAT/SOCIAL/EXPLORATION/PUZZLE/MIXED. Needed for the balance check (not all nodes should be COMBAT). Scene type: Cmb=combat (battle), Soc=social (dialogue/intrigue), Exp=exploration (exploration/travel), Puz=puzzle (riddle/mechanism), Mix=mixed (several types at once). Needed for the balance check — not all nodes should be Cmb.

situation.description: Situation description: what is here, who wants what, what state the world is in. NOT a "first A, then B" script — a static description from which the turn planner will draw an action.

hintsOut.description: Hints leading FROM this node to others (by the textIds of other nodes or a direct description). At least 1, for key nodes — ≥3 (the rule of three hints).

ifSkipped.description: What changes in the world if the node is skipped or destroyed (NPC killed/compressed, location destroyed). The turn planner uses this to move the node's function to another available node.

locationTextId.description: textId of the related location (`locations[*].textId`), if the node requires a developed map/setting/POI. Required for final COMBAT nodes and complex tactical scenes; for simple SOCIAL (dialogue) — null.

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description: Add a random-event table (class B events): rumors in public places, random encounters on the route, complications along the way. At least 4 rows, usually 6 (for a d6). Each row must seed the plot OR reveal the world OR telegraph a threat. If the book has no random events — `completeTask("add-random-tables")`. Closes on the first call.
name: addRandomTable

name.description: Title: "Rumors at the Port", "Encounters on the Road to the Monastery", "Complications in the Fire Citadel".

category.description: Table category (see [AiBookRandomTableCategory]). Random-event table category: Rum=rumors in public places (tavern, market, guardhouse — seed the plot, draw NPC characters); Enc=random encounters on the route (another party, a wandering NPC, a creature with a motive — not a "monster for the sake of combat"); Cmp=complications (weather/environment/moral choice/obstacle — makes the road lively).

applicableNodeTextIds.description: textIds of the nodes where this table applies. Empty list = global (for example, general rumors about the BB are available everywhere).

rows.description: Table rows — at least 4, usually 6 (for a d6 roll). Each must seed the plot OR reveal the world OR telegraph a threat.

rollValue.description: Roll value: 1, 2, 3... for d6/d20. If the table has no rolls (the planner chooses) — null.

content.description: What happens/what the players hear. 1-2 sentences. Concrete — no "something strange happens".

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description: Record a new task for yourself as a result of self-review. Available ONLY in the SELF_REVIEW phase. After adding all tasks call transitionTo into the working phase — the frame will execute them there.
name: addTask

description.description: What exactly needs to be done

description: FULL RESET: reset all the accumulated structure state (metadata/antagonist/nodes/encounters/items/locations/random tables/hints/descriptions) and reopen initialBuildTasks. Use ONLY in REGENERATE mode — FULL REBUILD ON INSPIRATION (the builder was preloaded with the old structure, there is no player request). After clearAll build the book from scratch as in initial generation, using the structure you just saw in the snapshot as **inspiration** (you may reuse names/setting/ideas). Do NOT call clearAll in IMPROVE mode (when there are adjustments from the player) — there pinpoint edits via update*/remove* are needed.
name: clearAll

textId.description: Slug identifier of the antagonist, format [a-z0-9-]+. Unique; used by hints/encounters/items for references (`relatedTextIds`/`npcTextId` etc.) the same way as textId of keyNpcs/nodes.

name.description: Name/title of the antagonist. Unique, may be conventional if the BB is an organization/phenomenon ("The Cult of the Nameless", "Winter").

description.description: BB description: who it is, what it looks like, how the party learns about it. Several sentences, no stats/CR.

motive.description: Motive: what it wants and WHY. Must be understandable and (ideally) not banally villainous. "Revenge for an executed brother", "does not want its native element to vanish", not "wants to rule the world".

resources.description: Antagonist resources: what it has at its disposal (minions, artifacts, factions, information). Brief, without stat blocks.

timeline.description: BB plan timeline: what will happen without the party's intervention. Each step — what and under which conditions/time. At least 3 steps for a five-beat arc.

trigger.description: Step trigger: time or condition. "After 3 days of inaction", "after the key witness dies", "when the party uncovers the first ritual".

event.description: What happens at this step. A concrete event that changes the game world. "A victim in the main square", "a second cultist arrives with reinforcements".

onDefeat.description: Reaction to the party's defeat/retreat: what the BB will do if the party fails on the first attempt or retreats altogether. Not "returns and kills everyone", but concretely: "goes underground, a season later raises a cult in the neighboring city".

profile.description: A profile WITHOUT NUMBERS: signature traits + relative danger in one or two phrases. "An elite shadow assassin — hits hard from stealth, fragile himself, relies on ambush". "A dim-witted brute — lots of health, slow, hits like a hammer". NO CR/HP/AC/damage — the turn master computes those to fit the party's strength.

scale.description: Relative scale of presence (NOT an absolute number): SOLO — a loner/boss; FEW — a small group; MANY — a noticeable crowd; SWARM — a swarm of minions. The exact number is chosen by the turn master to fit the player side's strength. Relative scale (no numbers): So=solo/boss; Fw=few/small group; Mn=many/crowd; Sw=swarm/swarm of minions.

role.description: Role in battle (exactly one word in Latin letters): "boss", "lieutenant", "minion", "support", "summon", "ally". This is the participant's canon, not an ornament: the turn master builds the enemy's role in battle from it, and "minion" is a minor role: a SWARM unit (one sheet represents a crowd) or a specific unit with its own role, not a clone extra. Set "minion" by its place in the battle, not as a filler by number.

motive.description: The participant's motive: what they want in this scene (besides "kill the heroes"). "Finish the ritual", "prevent escape", "hold out until help arrives", "protect the master". Makes behavior rounded, not just "attacks".

synergies.description: New synergies (replaces entirely; "X reinforces Y" links between participants)

lossCondition.description: New lossCondition (the loss condition in the scene, not to be confused with stakes)

twist.description: New twist; pass an object to replace, null = leave untouched

event.description: What happens: enemy reinforcements, a roof collapse, a third party appearing, an ally's mask being revealed. 1-2 sentences.

trigger.description: Trigger condition: "the alarm is raised", "the battle lasts >5 rounds", "an NPC drops below 50% HP", "a rune is activated", "the party is close to victory". Precise at the end, so the planner understands when to introduce it.

description.description: Phase description: what happens, what the task is, what the choices are. 1-3 sentences.

condition.description: Condition for transitioning into this phase. For the first — null/"battle start"; for subsequent ones — a concrete trigger: "when the boss's HP <50%", "when the shield crystal is destroyed", "after round 5", "when one of the minions ran off for reinforcements".

effect.description: What changes in the arena/encounter on switching: new opponents appear, hazards activate, access to a POI opens, terrain changes (the bridge collapsed). Concretely — what the planner must change in the scene.
